subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should plain provider text like `LLM error api_error: Internal server error` be classified for cron and fallback behavior?
rationale: The code shows this is not a regex-only fix because each classification changes retry matching, fallback timing, and whether provider/auth-profile health is affected during cron runs.

options.title: Map to server_error with cron-local handling
options.body: Use the existing `server_error` reason for plain provider 500s, avoid shared auth-profile poisoning by default, and require tests for cron fallback, retry, and alert timing.

options.title: Map to overloaded
options.body: Skip same-provider candidates sooner, but require explicit proof that generic HTTP 500s do not broadly poison provider/profile health for other healthy workloads.

options.title: Keep timeout semantics
options.body: Leave plain 500s as timeout and solve the missed-window behavior with per-candidate or first-progress budgets instead of a new outage classification.

recommendation.title: Map to server_error with cron-local handling
recommendation.body: Use the existing `server_error` reason for plain provider 500s, avoid shared auth-profile poisoning by default, and require tests for cron fallback, retry, and alert timing.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate from the merged structured server-error retry path and review/merge context.
